name: Substation and transformer overheating
blurb: Property cover for high voltage failures caused by sudden AI workload spikes.
summary: Property cover for high voltage failures caused by sudden AI workload spikes.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: Aggregation creep: the carrier bundles separate transformer failures across two buildings on a shared campus into a single occurrence or a single aggregate sublimit. Insist on per building occurrence definitions and deductibles.

Notice prejudice trap: the carrier denies because telemetry logged partial discharge advisories weeks before the failure and the operator did not notify. Restrict notice triggers to actual physical failure, not predictive maintenance alerts.
Consent or hammer clauses: the carrier pushes a low settlement with a salvage vendor and penalises the operator for choosing OEM certified long lead transformer replacement instead.

Utility tariff liability caps versus insurance drop down: the carrier argues the operator contractually assumed liability beyond legal limits through the interconnection agreement. Needs a broad contractual liability endorsement covering tariff flow throughs.
Fluorinated greenhouse gas or emerging chemical exclusions drafted broadly enough to deny defence costs for SF6 arc byproduct exposure.

Cross liability exclusion stripping cover when one hyperscale tenant or utility partner on a shared campus sues another. Delete it, or restrict it to disputes between named insured corporate entities.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Ensuing loss carve back: notwithstanding any exclusion for wear and tear, gradual thermal degradation or insulation aging, the policy covers all ensuing catastrophic destruction, arc flash, oil boil over, fire or terminal short resulting from it.

Predictive telemetry notice immunisation: notice obligations and notice prejudice defences trigger solely on actual physical failure, rupture or fire. Predictive maintenance logs, partial discharge advisories and AI thermal anomaly alerts do not constitute constructive notice.

Aggregation clarification: a simultaneous or sequential multi building transient from a shared primary distribution bus is treated as separate occurrences per affected building, or as a single occurrence with a stated sublimit carve out, with the preference specified.
Redefined physical damage to include electronic bricking, thermal shock and melting of silicon during a sudden power or cooling failure, without requiring fire or structural collapse.
Actual replacement cost valuation with price markup protection for constrained secondary market sourcing, rather than a cap at original manufacturer price.
Broad form contractual liability extending to indemnity assumptions in the interconnection agreement, and cover for utility subrogation arising from grid transients.
Explosion and collapse cover with no blast exclusion for high voltage switchyards, and ensuing third party fire spread.
Third party toxic tort and environmental carve back so arc decomposition gas release is not treated as a gradual pollution exclusion.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: 12 operational hours is a representative request. Standard forms carry 24 to 48 hours, and for a training cluster that is the whole loss.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: 24 month indemnity period, against a standard 12 month cap, because custom transformers run 2 to 4 years and accelerators 6 to 18 months. Contingent business interruption for upstream fibre and regional transmission trunk trips included.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Self insured retention of 2,500,000 per occurrence is a representative proposal for a 120 MW campus. Valuation at actual replacement cost with the depreciation waiver stated: GPU nodes at 30,000 to 400,000 each, 230kV transformers at roughly 4.2 million per unit with a 36 month lead time, switchgear bays at 18 months.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: 500,000,000 per occurrence, layered primary and excess property and equipment breakdown, on non admitted surplus lines manuscript paper. High voltage transformer and switchgear physical damage at the full policy limit.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Standard 1,000,000 per occurrence and 2,000,000 aggregate is the typical primary. It is not the layer that matters for this exposure.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based for the property and equipment breakdown tower, triggered by physical destruction, arc flash, oil boil over or terminal electrical short during the policy period. Occurrence based for CGL and the excess or umbrella tower. Claims made applies to D&O and cyber, not here.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Scaled to 25 million to 150 million and higher where the campus shares a boundary with municipal, chemical or other critical industrial assets. Distinct from the property tower, which for a hyperscale facility runs to 500 million per occurrence on layered surplus lines paper.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Utility subrogation and grid backfeed: an internal arc flash or phase to ground fault in a private 230kV substation trips or damages the utility shared distribution bus, and the utility carrier subrogates against the operator.
Blast wave, shrapnel and fire spread across the fence line from a transformer rupture or oil boil over onto neighbouring industrial, commercial or residential property.

Toxic arc decomposition byproducts: SF6 or alternative dielectric gas under high voltage arcing breaks down into thionyl fluoride, sulfur dioxide and hydrofluoric acid, vented through pressure relief, creating third party inhalation and environmental claims.
Third party bodily injury to contractors, utility escorts and perimeter workers from step and touch potential gradients or arc flash thermal radiation.

underwriter_wants_to_know: High voltage commissioning evidence that extends past the low voltage switchboard: switchgear test records, protection study verifications, and utility grid compliance documentation. Records that stop at the LV board are treated as a disqualifier.
A design stage protection philosophy documenting the interface between the private substation and the utility distribution network, and how a fault is prevented from cascading in either direction.
A protective relay coordination study to IEEE or IEC standards showing selective isolation of transformer primary and secondary fault currents, and anti-backfeed isolation toward the utility.

Thermal and power surge telemetry proving that chillers, cooling loops and switchgear absorb a 100 percent step load spike from GPU workloads without arc flash or thermal runaway, validated through BMS or DCIM logs.
A fully executed utility interconnection agreement with explicit indemnification boundaries, since the liability side of a substation loss turns on what was contractually assumed.
An NFPA 70E arc flash hazard analysis, blast walls, and oil containment sumps sized for the full transformer volume plus suppression discharge.

Closed loop SF6 density and pressure monitoring, zero emission gas reclamation certification, and leakage logs compliant with EPA and CARB rules, because arc decomposition byproducts are a third party toxic exposure.
